children: new CEO, John Ternus, indicated he is focused on building the best devices rather than entering the AI model race, according to
, which named the new iPhone Duo as one of the best inventions of 2026.
No matter what frontier AI lab develops the most capable and user-friendly chatbot, consumers will still want to use those on an iPhone, he contends. So while Google
pour a combined hundreds of billions into model development, Apple has taken a different approach.

"People want physical things," he said, according to the report. "They want to talk, to see images of loved ones, to take pictures. So I don't see a scenario where all of a sudden, our devices disappear and we don't have a need for an iPhone."
Greg Joswiak, Apple's senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing agrees.
"We don't feel threatened," Joswiak said. "The fact that we can do the integration means we can create just a better experience than anybody else."
"You can't do everything," Ternus added. "So we kind of try to constrain ourselves to the stuff that matters most—and then put all of our effort into those things."
So far, the iPhone Duo has received a barrage of positive reviews. Samsung's
Galaxy Z Fold 8 has experienced strong demand, especially in Asia, suggesting a growing market for foldables despite the high price tag. The iPhone Duo starts at $2,000.

title: Apple's Ternus retains focus on hardware rather than creating AI model of the month: report
